title: Orcas Keep Sinking Sailboats Off Spain, and Never Touch the Crew

scenes.text: Since 2020, orcas have been sinking boats. Nobody has been hurt.
It began in the Strait of Gibraltar in May 2020. Orcas started swimming up behind sailboats and going for one part.
The rudder. They ram it, bite it and snap it, sometimes spinning the whole boat around.
More than 500 run-ins have been reported, and several yachts have gone to the bottom. Every time, the crew got off unharmed.
Only about fifteen orcas have been seen doing it, in a critically endangered group of roughly forty.
Revenge makes a better headline, but researchers see no sign of aggression. Their best guess: the young ones are playing, and it spread like a fad.

description:
Since May 2020 a small group of orcas around the Strait of Gibraltar has been ramming sailboats and breaking their rudders. More than 500 interactions have been reported and several boats have sunk, yet no person has been harmed.
About fifteen individuals from a critically endangered population of roughly forty take part, mostly juveniles; researchers who study them see no aggressive intent and lean towards play or a cultural fad.
Play or payback: what do you think the orcas are doing?
subject: orca killer whale
first_comment: Most encounters are over in under half an hour, and about half leave the boat damaged. Would you still sail through the Strait of Gibraltar?
